title.narrative: Power of Voices – Benkadi

description.narrative: Benkadi is a civil society initiative that aims to improve the effectiveness of public policies for climate change adaption and mitigation of climate change effects in West Africa through more inclusive governance. Benkadi is a consortium with a structure that supports southern leadership, in which the South has taken initiative and ownership and ensures end-user representation in the decision-making processes related to climate change.

In a written consultation on the budget for 2022, when Benkadi was mentioned by the Dutch minister of foreign trade and development cooperation on climate actions in Benin and Ivory Coast as an example of local partnership. Second, Dutch politicians included the voices of citizens in the debate in 2022 was on 17 February, with the ‘adopt an SDG’ event in which a representation of Dutch parliamentarians discussed about the international effects of climate change with a focus on local ownership and development for the most vulnerable . Third achievement was the debate on the government policy paper on development cooperation where climate adaptation and policy coherence have both emerged as very important themes. Woord en Daad with partners (Partos and Building Change) have significantly contributed to lobbying for this emphasis.

Realisation 2025: * Resolution EP on COP30 called for meaningful participation of CSOs at COP30 * in a KGG committee debate, MPs questioned Minister Hermans about CSO involvement at COP30
Overview 2021 - 2025 realisation: Dutch politicians in both the Dutch and the European Parliament, from left to right, were presented the Benkadi manifesto on several occasions in 2024 and 2025. All politicians demonstrated a commitment to include the messages from the manifesto on policy coherence, climate finance and equal partnerships with Africa, in decision-making. Examples and stories from West Africa, shared by the partners from Benin, Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso, underlined the importance of climate action and a continuing commitment from NL and EU. End of October, 2025, a resolution was adopted in the European Parliament reflecting some of our main points – including the need for additional climate finance (grant-based, accessible) and policy coherence. In september 2025, the Benkadi partners together organised a public conference in The Hague, bringing together experts and decision-makers around the topic of climate justice, including from the Advisory Council International Affairs, the Ministry of Climate and Green Growth, and from the Dutch and EU Parliaments. The Southern partners brought the West African experiences and challenges into the discussions, underling the urgency of joint climate action and solidarity with West Africa. Politicians promised to include this perspective in their deliberations on related topics. The Reformed Daily published an article on the conference.

comment.narrative: The voices of West African citizens have been meaningfully included in debates and resolutions three times in 2023. (1) A politician from CU has specifically referred to Benkadi in her speech in the Dutch national parliament. She mentioned Benkadi and specific topics including as coastal erosion, floodings and droughts. This was linked to the effects on vulnerable groups such as women and girls. (2) Benkadi NL/EU lobbied for a resolution concerning the water sector that was adopted. It specifically anchors the Dutch commitment for a focus on serving women and girls in the most vulnerable areas. (3) The Dutch parliament adopted a resolution concerning participatory research on neglated and underutilized climate-resilience coprs in the least developed countries. Here the effects of polices on climate change in West Africa have been taken into account.

comment.narrative: No Dutch or European laws are taking into account the situation of West African citizens vulnerable to the effects of climate change.

In general, by 2025 West African citizens vulnerable to the effects of climate change have been crucial in relevant laws/policies (by effective implementation of SDG-toets. Concretely: 1. Woord en Daad (WD) contributes to an improvement of the focus on climate adaptation and policy coherence in the policy paper of the ministry of foreign trade and development cooperation, adopted in 2022. 2. WD contributes to an improvement international climate strategy (to be adopted 2023) of the Dutch government, with in particular the perspective of West-African countries. 3. WD contributes to an improved focus on food security for West-African citizens vulnerable to climate change in the overall Africa Strategy (to be debated and adopted in 2023) 4. Annual budgets which are technically very concrete laws, show an improved commitment of the Dutch government on climate adaptation in West-African countries. Subsidy frameworks allocate sufficient financial resources for this purpose.

comment.narrative: In 2022, one result was achieved with the government policy paper ‘Doen waar Nederland goed in is’, to which Woord en Daad with partners (Partos and Building Change) have significantly contributed through lobbying for an improved emphasis on climate adaptation and policy coherence. Also groundwork was done to achieve the other objectives for 2025. Notably on raising the importance of the theme of climate adaptation through the Food4All coalition and Building Change and also Woord en Daad’s own position paper Netherlands’ Global Climate Strategy for the members of Parliament’s Committee on BH-OS. Also Woord en Daad has initiated and chaired several round tables in which Dutch and (West-)African civil society organizations could give input on the upcoming Africa strategy. Though still approved, in this strategy, food security will be concretely linked with climate change to which these round table consultations contributed. Also preparations for the NL climate strategy and a visit of a Dutch parliamentary visit to Benin were done.

comment.narrative: In 2023, 1 result was achieved on the second component targeted: The Dutch Global Climate Strategy was published with “a new approach of providing direct support to the poorest countries in Sub-Saharan Africa”. According to the strategy, government's efforts will be “primarily targeted at vulnerable areas and ‘climate hotspots’” in (..) Africa, with particular focus on climate resilience for smallholder farmers in the Sahel, which is precisely what we have been advocating for, including during preparations of the parliamentary debate (March 30). Finally, “coastal cities vulnerable to rising sea levels” are explicitly mentioned (Benin, Ivory Coast) in the strategy, as well as a firm anchoring of the link between climate change, biodiversity loss, and land degradation, with all its consequences for vulnerable food systems in the Sahel and West-Africa. Meanwhile preparatory advocacy was done for 3, to be materialized in the international agriculture, nature and food strategy and, with likeminded organisations, advocacy is done for result 4, for which the budgets will be discussed in early 202

comment.narrative:
2025 realisation: Resolution adopted in EP on EU's ambition for COP30, including a call to ensure meaningful involvement of CSOs at COP30
Overview 2021-2025: In 2025, West African citizens vulnerable to climate change have influenced public discourse and policy debates on development cooperation and international climate strategy. Through Benkadi’s advocacy, issues such as soil degradation, coastal erosion, and the link between climate impacts and insecurity in the Sahel have gained visibility among policymakers and opinion leaders—strengthening Woord en Daad’s voice in shaping priorities. Woord en Daad contributed directly to the Schreinemacher policy (2022) by providing evidence on climate adaptation needs, ensuring that adaptation targets were included alongside food and water security objectives. In 2023, Woord en Daad engaged in consultations for the Dutch International Climate Strategy, emphasizing West Africa’s vulnerability and securing language on private climate investment mobilization. Similarly, during the Africa Strategy debate, Woord en Daad advocated for integrating food security for climate-affected communities, resulting in stronger alignment between adaptation and agricultural resilience. Despite setbacks under the Klever policy (2025)—where climate budgets were reduced and mainstreamed—Woord en Daad maintained influence through continuous dialogue with the Ministry and EU actors. For example, recent exchanges with the European Commission helped keep West Africa on the strategic agenda, even as standalone climate targets disappeared from the Multiannual Financial Framework. Concrete outcomes reflect this advocacy: Dutch investments in water and food security will rise in Benin in 2026, and Côte d’Ivoire will receive significant climate-resilient infrastructure funding through Invest International. Woord en Daad also pushed for localization ambitions within the Africa Strategy, ensuring better alignment of food security efforts for vulnerable citizens. While accelerating the International Climate Strategy remains politically unfeasible, Woord en Daad’s contributions have safeguarded adaptation priorities, mobilized private investments, and maintained West Africa’s prominence in Dutch and EU policy frameworks.
